reason: Selected retrieval ablation supports testing complementary channels; broad provenance and substrate-causality claims are not isolated by this ablation.

candidates.title: Compare hybrid and single-channel memory retrieval
candidates.rule: For provenance-backed conversational memory, compare combined lexical and embedding retrieval with each channel alone before choosing the retrieval interface.
candidates.finding: With the fixed gpt-5.6-sol backbone, hybrid retrieval scores 95.20% on LongMemEval versus 94.00% embedding-only, 93.40% lexical-only and 93.60% grep-only. This isolates the channel interface in the authors’ system.
models: gpt-5.6-sol as named by the paper
candidates.conditions: All other components remain fixed; searches operate over multiple provenance-aware stores.
candidates.limitations: Small absolute gains without inspected confidence intervals or repeated-seed results. This does not isolate provenance, three-store design or citation locks as causes. Published competitor figures are not necessarily controlled reruns.
candidates.validation_test: Compare channels on independent questions with identical reader and budget, including identifiers and paraphrases; report QA, recall, false citations and incremental latency.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
